record.original_question: Characterize exactly which pairs of rooted polytopes have a mix that is itself polytopal rather than merely a rooted maniplex.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Give a characterization of pairs of rooted polytopes whose mix is itself a polytope.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function having range {-1, 0, ..., n}, with a unique minimum face F_{-1} and unique maximum face F_n, such that every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 faces, P is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: whenever F < G with rank(G) − rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. For each i ∈ {0, 1, ..., n−1} and each flag Φ of P there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face.

A maniplex of rank n is a combinatorial generalization of a polytope: it is an n-edge-colored connected graph whose vertices represent flags and whose i-colored edges represent the i-adjacency, satisfying the same local conditions as the flag graph of a polytope, but without requiring the existence of an underlying poset. Every abstract polytope gives rise to a maniplex via its flag graph, but not every maniplex arises this way.

A rooted polytope (resp. rooted maniplex) is a pair (P, Φ) where P is an abstract polytope (resp. maniplex) and Φ is a distinguished base flag of P. For each i, let r_i denote the involution that sends a flag to its i-adjacent flag. The monodromy group Mon(P) is the group generated by r_0, ..., r_{n−1} acting on the flags of P.

Given two rooted polytopes (P_1, Φ_1) and (P_2, Φ_2) of the same rank n, their mix (P_1 ◇ P_2, (Φ_1, Φ_2)) is the rooted maniplex defined as follows. Consider the subgroup of Mon(P_1) × Mon(P_2) generated by the diagonal elements (r_i^{P_1}, r_i^{P_2}) for i = 0, ..., n−1. The flags of the mix are the orbits of the base flag pair (Φ_1, Φ_2) under this group, with i-adjacency given by the diagonal generators. The mix is always a rooted maniplex, but it need not be the flag graph of an abstract polytope.

Problem:

Give a complete characterization of those pairs of rooted polytopes (P_1, Φ_1), (P_2, Φ_2) for which the mix (P_1 ◇ P_2, (Φ_1, Φ_2)) is itself (the flag graph of) an abstract polytope, rather than merely a rooted maniplex.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned no evidence of a published characterization of when the mix of two rooted polytopes is polytopal. Related recent work focuses on automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes and two-orbit polytopes, but does not address this specific characterization, suggesting the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes (arXiv preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Presents 35 open problems on combinatorial, geometric and algebraic aspects of k-orbit abstract polytopes, together with a theory of rooted polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The mix-polytopality characterization is listed among open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes via coset geometries but does not address mixing of rooted polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on k-orbit polytopes does not resolve the mix characterization.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: A structural theory of two-orbit polytopes describing their face-transitivity and automorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent structural work on two-orbit polytopes does not provide a polytopality criterion for mixes.
